Georgia|occupied territories]] }} '''Georgia'''{{efn|{{Lang-ka|საქართველო|tr}}, {{IPA|ka|sakʰartʰʷelo|IPA|Sakartvelo.ogg}}}} is a country in the [[Caucasus]] region on the east coast of the [[Black Sea]]. It is located at the intersection of [[Eastern Europe]] and [[West Asia]][[Encyclopedia Britannica]]", [https://www.britannica.com/place/Caucasus Caucasus] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200504123439/https://www.britannica.com/place/Caucasus |date=4 May 2020 }}, June 2021: "One widely accepted scheme draws the dividing line along the crest of the Greater Caucasus range, putting the portion of the region north of the line in Europe and the portion south of it in Asia. Another puts the western portion of the Caucasus region in Europe and the eastern part (the bulk of Azerbaijan and small portions of Armenia, Georgia, and Russia's Caspian Sea coast) in Asia..."''[[Histories (Herodotus)|Histories]]'' 4.38. Cf. James Rennell, ''The geographical system of Herodotus examined and explained'', Volume 1, Rivington 1830, [[iarchive:bub gb enQ-AAAAcAAJ/page/n274|p. 244]]{{efn|For a more complete explanation, see: [[Boundaries between the continents]]}} and is generally regarded as part of Europe.Encyclopedic World Atlas, George Philip & Son, [[Oxford University Press]]: 2002, p.104 It is bordered to the north and northeast by [[Russia]]; to the west by the Black Sea, to the south by [[Turkey]] and [[Armenia]], and to the southeast by [[Azerbaijan]]. It has a population of 3.9 million,{{efn|This figure excludes Abkhazia and South Ossetia, two [[Russian-occupied territories in Georgia|Russian-occupied]] territories of Georgia that only Russia and a [[List of states with limited recognition|small number of other countries]] recognize. The [[Government of Georgia (country)|government of Georgia]] considers the two areas as integral parts of the country, with [[International recognition of Abkhazia and South Ossetia|international support]].}} of which over a third live in [[Tbilisi]], the capital and largest city. [[Georgians]], who are native to the region and constitute the majority of the population, are ethno-linguistically distinct from their neighboring nations and primarily speak [[Georgian language|Georgian]], a [[Kartvelian language]] that has no relation to any other language family in the world.{{sfn|Dalby|2002|p=38}} Georgia has been inhabited since prehistory and is known for hosting the world's earliest known sites of [[wine]]making.{{cite news |title='World's oldest wine' found in 8,000-year-old jars in Georgia |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-41977709 |work=BBC News |date=13 November 2017 |archive-date=14 November 2017 |access-date=8 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171114041222/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-41977709 |url-status=live }}{{cite journal |last1=Guerra-Doce |first1=Elisa |title=The Origins of Inebriation: Archaeological Evidence of the Consumption of Fermented Beverages and Drugs in Prehistoric Eurasia |journal=Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory |date=September 2015 |volume=22 |issue=3 |pages=751–782 |doi=10.1007/s10816-014-9205-z }} The [[Classical antiquity|classical era]] saw the emergence of several kingdoms, such as [[Colchis]] and [[Kingdom of Iberia|Iberia]], that formed the nucleus of the modern Georgian state. In the early 4th century, Georgians officially [[Christianization of the Kingdom of Iberia|adopted Christianity]], which contributed to [[Unification of the Georgian realm|their unification]] under the [[Kingdom of Georgia]]. Georgia reached [[Georgian Golden Age|its Golden Age]] during the [[High Middle Ages]] under the reigns of King [[David IV]] and his great-granddaughter [[Tamar of Georgia|Tamar]]. Beginning in the 15th century, the kingdom [[Collapse of the Georgian realm|declined and disintegrated]] under relentless attacks from hostile empires like the [[Mongol Empire|Mongols]], the [[Ottoman Empire]], and [[History of Iran|Persia]]. Georgia requested support from the [[Russian Empire]], which ended up [[Georgia within the Russian Empire|gradually annexing]] the country starting in 1801. After the [[Russian Revolution]] in 1917, Georgia briefly emerged as [[Democratic Republic of Georgia|an independent republic]] under [[Treaty of Poti|German protection]].{{Cite journal |last=Jones |first=Stephen |date=27 October 2020|title=The establishment of Soviet power in Transcaucasia: The case of Georgia 1921–1928|journal=Soviet Studies|volume=40|issue=4|page=627 |doi=10.1080/09668138808411783}} However, the country was [[Soviet invasion of Georgia|invaded and annexed]] by the [[Red Army]] in 1921; it then became a [[Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic|republic of the Soviet Union]]. In the 1980s, an independence movement grew quickly, leading to [[Dissolution of the Soviet Union|Georgia's secession from the Soviet Union]] in April 1991. For much of the [[Post-Soviet states|subsequent decade]], the country endured economic crises, [[List of conflicts in territory of the former Soviet Union|political instability]], and secessionist wars in [[Abkhazia]] and [[South Ossetia]]. Following the peaceful [[Rose Revolution]] in 2003, Georgia strongly pursued a [[Western world|pro-Western]] foreign policy, introducing a series of [[Potential enlargement of the European Union|reforms aimed at integration]] into the [[European Union]] and [[Enlargement of NATO|NATO]]. This Western orientation led to [[Georgia–Russia relations|worsening relations with Russia]], culminating in the [[Russo-Georgian War]] of 2008 and continued Russian occupation of [[Russian-occupied territories in Georgia|parts of Georgia]]. Georgia is a [[representative democracy]] governed as a [[unitary state|unitary]] [[parliamentary republic]].{{cite web |title=Constitution of Georgia |at=Article 1.1, 7.2, 45, 52 and 54 |url=https://matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/30346?publication=36 |publisher=The Legislative Herald of Georgia |date=29 June 2020 |access-date=2022-03-25 |archive-date=27 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231027061907/https://matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/30346?publication=36 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=https://www.ge.undp.org/content/georgia/en/home/projects/PARLIAMENT.html |title=Consolidating Parliamentary Democracy in Georgia |publisher=UNDP Georgia |access-date=2022-03-25 |archive-date=19 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210619184258/https://www.ge.undp.org/content/georgia/en/home/projects/PARLIAMENT.html }} It is a [[developing country]] with a very high [[List of countries by Human Development Index|Human Development Index]] and an [[emerging market]] economy. Sweeping economic reforms since 2003 have resulted in one of the [[Ease of doing business index|freest business climates]] in the world, as well as greater [[Economic Freedom of the World|economic freedom]] and [[Global Corruption Barometer|transparency]].{{Cite web |title=Georgia |url=https://www.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/georgia/ |access-date=2024-07-21 |website=United States Department of State |language=en-US |archive-date=18 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718133937/https://www.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/georgia/ |url-status=live }} In 2018, Georgia became the second country [[Cannabis in Georgia (country)|to legalize cannabis]], and the first former socialist state to do so. Georgia is a member of numerous international organizations, including the [[Council of Europe]], [[Eurocontrol]], [[Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation|BSEC]], [[GUAM Organization for Democracy and Economic Development|GUAM]], and [[Energy Community]]. As part of the [[Association Trio]], Georgia is an official candidate for [[Potential enlargement of the European Union|membership in the European Union]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/european-council/2023/12/14-15/|title=European Council|website=Consilium|date=26 October 2023|access-date=15 December 2023|archive-date=3 July 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250703042603/https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/european-council/2023/12/14-15/|url-status=live}} Since October 2024, Georgia has been immersed in a [[2024–2026 Georgian political crisis|deep political crisis]].
